title: Whole Product
equation: Whole Product = (Core Product + Integrations + Services + Support + References) ÷ 5
hook: Your product can be great and still lose because customers have to figure out everything around it.
statement: Mainstream customers buy a complete solution, not just your core product.
explainer: Early fans will piece things together themselves. Most buyers won't. If they need setup, training, integrations, or support to succeed, they'll buy from whoever packages all of it.
sop: List everything a customer needs to succeed beyond your core product.
For each gap, decide to build, buy, or partner.
Bundle it all into one complete offer.
Update the bundle as expectations rise.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Core Product 9, Integrations 4, Services 3, Support 6, References 5. (9 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 5) ÷ 5 = 5.4. Higher means customers get everything from you. Lower means they're assembling the rest, and might buy elsewhere.
question: List three things your customers still have to figure out on their own after buying.
closing_statement: Customers buy outcomes, not the core feature alone.
caption:
